4	
5	# Architectural decisions
6	
7	Project-wide decisions for MD². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.
8	
9	## File naming
10	
11	| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |
14	
15	## Services and state
16	
17	| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
20	| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
21	| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
22	| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |
23	
24	## Card state
25	
26	| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
29	| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
30	| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |
31	
32	
33	## Events and React integration
34	
35	| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
36	| --- | --- | --- |
37	| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
38	| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
39	| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
40	| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

50	# General feature description
51	
52	The user should be able to attach a json list (file) to an action so it will run the same action in a loop on the card where each iteration in the loop is for a record in that list (the record becomes a part of the context for the conversation). All editors that can contain placeholders can then also have the 'data' placeholder, which has a second part for selecting the value in the json data.
53	
54	* On the agent-action-popup, we have a context menu (prompt menu) that currently contains 2 menu items: `compact` & `add file` , we need to add 'for-each' here, which allows the user to select 1 json file that will be attached to the conversation as the 'for-each' data
55	* the placeholder looks like: `{{data xx.xx.x.xx}}` example `{{data countries.0.cities}}` so countries is a list, we take the item at index 0, field 'cities'
56	* when an action has a 'for-each' file attached, show a `loop` icon behind the action label in the action button at the top of the action popup. (the loop icon should be something like a horizontal 8)
57	* also show the loop icon in front of the 'prompt menu' button (vertical dots) that opens the prompt's context menu. The loop icon also opens a context menu where the user can configure the for-each:
58	  * remove: remove the json file and thus the loop
59	  * view: view the contents of the json file (external open)
60	  * at end: sub menu where user can select exclusively out of:
61	    * add prompt: add the next record as a new prompt to the same conversation
62	    * compact: when enabled, after every record in the json file, compact 
63	    * new conversation: start a new conversation for each record
64	  * on failure: sub menu where user can select exclusively out of:
65	    * log and continue: log the failure in the conversation and continue with the next record
66	    * stop on first failure: log the failure and stop the loop
67	* if the file only contains an object, than that becomes 1 record. if it contains a list, all items in that list are traversed.
68	* The electron app is responsible for performing the loop.
69	
70	## Current state
71	
72	The prompt menu currently supports `Compact` and `Add file`. `Add file` copies selected files through the attachment workflow and inserts Markdown links; it does not create loop input.
73	
74	Action prompt placeholders come from one fixed list. Electron resolves those placeholders once, then executes one action run. Conversation records persist in activity JSON and survive popup and application restarts, but they do not contain for-each data or settings.
75	
76	## implementation details
77	
78	- Support for-each only for agent-action popup conversations. Keep it out of action definitions.
79	- Add `For each` to `ActionPromptMenu`. Accept one `.json` file, parse it before the run starts, and reject invalid JSON without changing the conversation.
80	- Store the attached file name, JSON value, loop mode, and failure policy on the conversation. Send this data as run-specific input when creating the conversation; Electron validates and persists it with the canonical conversation record. Reloading the conversation restores the loop configuration.
81	- Treat a root JSON object as one record. Treat a root array as its ordered records. An empty array completes without starting an agent turn.
82	- Add `{{data <path>}}` to every editor that uses action placeholders. Resolve `<path>` against the current record using dot-separated object keys and zero-based array indexes, for example `{{data countries.0.cities}}`. Insert strings unchanged; serialize numbers, booleans, `null`, objects, and arrays as JSON. A missing path fails that record.
83	- Extend the renderer-to-Electron run-input contract and its validation with the conversation-owned for-each configuration. Keep parsing, iteration, placeholder resolution, cancellation, and failure handling in Electron.
84	- Run records sequentially. Do not start the next record until the previous agent turn and configured end behavior finish.
85	- Provide three mutually exclusive loop modes:
86	  - `add prompt` (default): run the first record in the conversation, then submit each later resolved prompt as another turn in that conversation;
87	  - `compact`: use the same conversation and compact it after each record before submitting the next record;
88	  - `new conversation`: create a separate conversation for every record.
89	- Provide two mutually exclusive failure policies:
90	  - `log and continue` (default): append a loop-failure event to the affected conversation and continue with the next record;
91	  - `stop on first failure`: record the failure and do not start later records.
92	- A user cancellation stops the active turn and prevents all remaining records from starting.
93	- Show a loop icon after the action label and before the prompt-menu button when the displayed conversation or new-conversation draft has for-each data. The icon opens a menu with `Remove`, `View`, loop mode, and failure policy. Disable configuration changes while the loop is running.
94	- `Remove` clears the conversation's for-each data and settings. `View` opens the persisted JSON content externally through Electron; it must not depend on the originally selected file still existing.
95	- Keep normal single-run behavior, action-definition validation, and non-agent actions unchanged.
96	- Add focused renderer tests for file selection, restored conversation state, icon/menu behavior, and submitted run input. Add shared-schema tests for persisted conversation data. Add Electron tests for record normalization, data-path resolution, all loop modes, both failure policies, cancellation, invalid JSON, empty arrays, and restart recovery.
97	
98	## acceptance criteria
99	
100	- User can attach exactly one JSON file from `For each` in an agent-action popup. Selecting another file replaces the current attachment only after the new file validates.
101	- Invalid JSON shows an error and leaves current conversation configuration unchanged.
102	- Attached data and selected settings survive closing and reopening the popup and restarting the application.
103	- Root object produces one iteration. Root array produces one iteration per item in source order. Empty root array starts no agent turn.
104	- `{{data <path>}}` resolves from the current record in every editor that supports action placeholders. Object keys and array indexes work; missing paths fail only the current record.
105	- Default mode runs the first record in the selected conversation and adds each later record as a new prompt in that same conversation.
106	- `compact` mode compacts the same conversation after each record before the next prompt starts.
107	- `new conversation` mode creates one conversation per record and never continues a previous record's conversation.
108	- Loop mode offers exactly one selected value: `add prompt`, `compact`, or `new conversation`.
109	- Failure policy defaults to `log and continue`. Each failed record adds a visible failure event to its conversation, and the next record starts.

27	
28	in the for-each config popup, user should be able to set the index position to start from, default 0.
29	
30	This should be passed on to the desktop with the rest of the for-each info.
31	
32	## Current state
33	
34	`ActionForEachConfig` stores the JSON value, file name, optional data path, end mode, and failure policy. Draft configuration lives in `ActionRunInputStore`; configuration on an existing conversation is persisted in its activity file. Shared validation rejects unknown fields, and the complete configuration reaches the desktop in the action run input.
35	
36	`ActionForEachSetupDialog` stages the existing settings until Save. It has no start-index field. `ActionRun.executeAgentForEach` resolves the ordered record list and always starts with record index `0`.
37	
38	## implementation details
39	
40	- Add `startIndex` to `ActionForEachConfig`. It is a zero-based, non-negative safe integer. Shared configuration validation must reject negative, fractional, unsafe, and non-number values. Treat a missing field as `0` so existing saved configurations retain current behavior, and return the normalized configuration with `startIndex` included.
41	- Add a numeric `Start index` field to `ActionForEachSetupDialog`. Initialize it from `config.startIndex ?? 0`, stage edits with the other settings, and include the number in the complete configuration saved through the existing draft or conversation path. Use input constraints for a minimum of `0` and whole-number steps, then validate on Save and show invalid input through `dialogService`; do not silently coerce it.
42	- Resolve `dataPath` before applying `startIndex`. The desktop must execute records from the configured position through the end, in source order. Failure events and other index-based reporting must retain each record's original zero-based index rather than renumbering the remaining records from `0`.
43	- A `startIndex` equal to or greater than the resolved record count produces an empty loop. Complete successfully without starting an agent turn, matching existing empty-list behavior.
44	- Extend focused tests for setup defaults, save/cancel, invalid values, draft and persisted-conversation retention, shared and run-request validation, execution from the chosen index, original failure indexes, root arrays, data-path-selected arrays, and indexes at or beyond the record count.
45	
46	## acceptance criteria
47	
48	- For-each setup contains a `Start index` numeric field whose default is `0`.
49	- Start index is zero-based: `0` processes every resolved record, while `2` starts with the third resolved record and then processes all later records in order.
50	- Saved start index is retained in draft runs and persisted conversations, including after reopening a conversation, and reaches the desktop with the rest of `ActionForEachConfig`.
51	- Existing configurations without `startIndex` behave as `startIndex: 0`.
52	- Negative, fractional, unsafe, and non-number start indexes show a clear error and start no agent turn.
53	- Start index is applied after data-path selection. Failure reporting keeps original record indexes.
54	- A start index equal to or greater than record count completes successfully without an agent turn.
55	- Existing View, Remove, running-loop locking, end modes, failure policies, data-path selection, and `{{data path}}` placeholder behavior remain unchanged.

1	# Placeholders
2	
3	{% raw %}
4	
5	Placeholders let one action definition work for every card. They are written as `{{name}}` and resolved on the desktop side, just before the process starts.
6	
7	| Placeholder | Resolves to |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| `{{card-file}}` | Path to the selected card's Markdown file. |
10	| `{{this-card}}` | Alias of `{{card-file}}`; the same path to the selected card's Markdown file. |
11	| `{{card-title}}` | Title of the selected card. |
12	| `{{card-prompt}}` | The extra text you typed in the action popup for this run. |
13	| `{{active-cards-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured working folder under the opened repository. Active cards are root-level Markdown files in this folder shown on the dashboard. |
14	| `{{worktree-folder}}` | Absolute path to the action execution checkout. |
15	| `{{repository-folder}}` | Absolute path to the opened repository. |
16	| `{{project-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured `project.projectFolder` under the opened repository. Equal to `{{repository-folder}}` when configuration is empty. |
17	| `{{releases-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured releases folder under the opened repository. |
18	| `{{actions-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured actions folder under the opened repository. Includes `project.projectFolder` when configured. |
19	| `{{diagram-file}}` | Output path for a diagram action. Available when the action has diagram output. |
20	| `{{parent-node}}` | Label of the selected item when running a child diagram action. |
21	| `{{diagram-changes}}` | Generated text from reviewed diagram edits when sending changes to an agent. |
22	| `{{version}}` | Free-form answer confirmed for the current action run. Linked actions use the same answer. |
23	| `{{conflict-file}}` | Path of the conflicted file the action was started for in the merge conflict dialog. |
24	| `{{conflict-files}}` | Paths of all files still conflicted in the merge conflict session, one per line. |
25	
26	They work in both `prompt` (agent actions) and `command` (command actions).
27	
28	## Using them
29	
30	In the prompt editor, type `{{` for a typeahead list, or insert one from the toolbar.
31	
32	```json
33	{
34	  "id": "fix-bug",
35	  "label": "Fix bug",
36	  "description": "Fix the bug described on the card",
37	  "type": "agent",
38	  "prompt": "Fix the bug described in {{card-file}}.\n\nExtra instructions: {{card-prompt}}"
39	}
40	```
41	
42	```json
43	{
44	  "id": "open-in-editor",
45	  "label": "Open in VS Code",
46	  "description": "Open the card file in VS Code",
47	  "type": "command",
48	  "command": "code {{card-file}}"
49	}
50	```
51	
52	## Notes
53	
54	- A card placeholder only resolves when the action runs with card context. Use `appliesTo` with `"kind": "card"` so an action that needs `{{card-file}}` or `{{this-card}}` is only offered where it makes sense.
55	- Diagram placeholders need diagram context. `{{diagram-file}}` also needs an output path, `{{parent-node}}` needs a selected item in a child diagram context, and `{{diagram-changes}}` needs reviewed changes from the editor.
56	- Conflict placeholders need merge-conflict context. `{{conflict-file}}` only resolves when the action was started for one file, not from **all remaining files**.
57	- `{{card-prompt}}` is empty when you run without typing anything. Write prompts that read fine either way.
58	- `{{version}}` requires a confirmed or explicitly supplied version. Without one, executable text fails before it runs.
59	- During linked-worktree actions, `{{repository-folder}}`, `{{project-folder}}`, `{{active-cards-folder}}`, and `{{actions-folder}}` remain under the opened repository. Only `{{worktree-folder}}` changes to the linked worktree.
60	- The diff command in project configuration supports the same six folder placeholders plus `{{commit}}`, `{{branch}}`, and `{{file}}`. For diffs, `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{repository-folder}}` both resolve to the opened repository.
61	- Custom agent profiles support `{{model}}` in `command` and `{{sessionId}}` in `resumeCommand`. Those are profile placeholders, not action placeholders.
62	
63	{% endraw %}
64	
65	See also: [Action definition](action-definition.md), [Diagrams](../guide/diagrams.md), [Cookbook](cookbook.md).
